definitions.name: Strictly positive common-binary-confounder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)=\{\widetilde P\in\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}^{\circ}:\mathcal L_{\widetilde P}(X,A,Y)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},\;Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\text{ almost surely},\;(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U),\;\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}\leq\Gamma_A\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x},\;\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}\leq\Gamma_A\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X,\;\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}\leq\Gamma_a\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x},\;\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}\leq\Gamma_a\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}\text{ for every }(a,x)\in\{0,1\}\times\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: Feasible binary-mixture root
definitions.construction: Let \(B=1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\).  Define \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)=r\) when \(\theta=1\), and \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)=2r/\{B+\sqrt{B^2+4(1-w)(\theta-1)r}\}\) when \(\theta\neq1\), with the continuous value used at removable cases.

definitions.name: Common-pair endpoint functionals
definitions.construction: Define \(q^-_{a,x}(w_0,w_1)=\min_{\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}}q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\) and \(q^+_{a,x}(w_0,w_1)=\max_{\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}}q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\).  Set \(H^-_x=q^-_{1,x}-q^+_{0,x}\), \(H^+_x=q^+_{1,x}-q^-_{0,x}\), \(\ell_x=\min_{D_{A,x}}H^-_x\), \(\upsilon_x=\max_{D_{A,x}}H^+_x\), \(L=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\ell_x\), and \(R=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\upsilon_x\).

definitions.name: Internal separate-posterior-pair outer relaxation
definitions.construction: \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_x\lambda_x\{\min_{D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}-\max_{D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}\}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_x\lambda_x\{\max_{D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}-\min_{D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}\}\), where the two extrema within braces may use different posterior pairs; \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}=[L_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{sep}}]\).  This is an internal outer relaxation of the common-binary-confounder class, not a published marginal-sensitivity model.

definitions.name: Degeneracy-aware semialgebraic certificate
definitions.construction: For fixed rational observed summaries and rational finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) splits each objective by the signs of \(\pi_x-w_{a,x}\) and by \(\Gamma_a=1\); evaluates the two exposure-odds boundary arcs, their endpoints, and the constant-\(U\) corners; adjoins the legal quadratic-root variables; saturates stationary ideals by every cleared denominator and branch-boundary polynomial; isolates generic interior roots by bivariate resultants and Sturm sequences; validates each isolated candidate by rational interval Newton tests and the original inequalities; and invokes cylindrical algebraic decomposition whenever a resultant vanishes identically or the stationary ideal is positive-dimensional.  For that fixed input it returns real-algebraic endpoint values, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates; it does not return a symbolic atlas over varying inputs.

definitions.name: Parametric cylindrical-algebraic atlas procedure
definitions.construction: For rational or real-algebraic observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\), \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) treats \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\in\mathcal B\) as parameters, eliminates the legal mixture-root and stationary variables, and performs parametric cylindrical algebraic decomposition over \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\) to return exact quantifier-free sign cells and algebraic optimizer strata.  Rational isolating intervals are returned only after a zero-dimensional specialization.

definitions.name: Rational common-confounder witness
definitions.construction: In one stratum, \(P^\star\) has \(p=1/2\), \(w_1=4/5\), \(w_0=1/5\), \((\mu_{1,1},\mu_{1,0})=(13/20,1/20)\), \((\mu_{0,1},\mu_{0,0})=(4/5,1/10)\), and \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)=(16,36,36)\).  Conditional on \((X,U)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) as independent Bernoulli variables with these risks, and draw \(A\) from the Bayes-compatible Bernoulli law determined by \(p,w_0,w_1\).  Direct substitution gives the exact feasibility identities \(r_1=(4/5)(13/20)+(1/5)(1/20)=53/100\), \(r_0=(1/5)(4/5)+(4/5)(1/10)=6/25\), \(\pi=1/2\), \(\operatorname{OR}(w_1,w_0)=16\), \(\operatorname{OR}(13/20,1/20)=247/7<36\), and \(\operatorname{OR}(4/5,1/10)=36\).  All eight conditional Bernoulli cell probabilities are strictly between zero and one, and \(\tau(P^\star)=\{(13/20+1/20)-(4/5+1/10)\}/2=-1/10\).

definitions.name: Worked exact certificate for the rational witness
definitions.construction: Let \(t=w_1\), \(W(t)=16t/(1+15t)=w_0\), and let \(F_a(t,z;\vartheta)=(1-w_a(t))(\vartheta-1)z^2+[1+(w_a(t)-r_a)(\vartheta-1)]z-r_a\), where \(w_1(t)=t\), \(w_0(t)=W(t)\), \(r_1=53/100\), and \(r_0=6/25\).  On this reverse arc, \(\pi-w_1>0\) and \(\pi-w_0<0\).  The lower branch is therefore \(H^-=q_1(1/36)-q_0(1/36)\), and its endpoint is the unique legal solution of \(F_1(t,z_1;1/36)=F_0(t,z_0;1/36)=0\) and \(d\{q_1(t;1/36)-q_0(t;1/36)\}/dt=0\) in \(t\in[251392284/10^9,251392285/10^9]\), \(z_1\in[688551450/10^9,688551451/10^9]\), and \(z_0\in[841040182/10^9,841040183/10^9]\); its pair obeys \(w_0\in[843088267/10^9,843088268/10^9]\) and \(L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9]\).  The upper branch is \(H^+=q_1(36)-q_0(36)\), and its endpoint is the unique legal solution of the analogous system at \(\vartheta=36\) in \(t\in[242967344/10^9,242967345/10^9]\), \(z_1\in[392390615/10^9,392390616/10^9]\), and \(z_0\in[10930193/10^9,10930194/10^9]\); its pair obeys \(w_0\in[837004844/10^9,837004845/10^9]\) and \(R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9]\).  Both are reverse-arc stationary candidates satisfying exactly \(w_0(1-w_1)=16w_1(1-w_0)\), while the inactive exposure inequality has slack \(16w_0(1-w_1)-w_1(1-w_0)=255w_1(1-w_0)>0\).  In every displayed box, \(0<z_a<1\), \(m_{a,1}=\vartheta z_a/\{1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\}\in(0,1)\), and \(r_a=(1-w_a)z_a+w_am_{a,1}\) hold with positive denominators.  Complementing \(U\) gives the second attaining pair and replaces \(\vartheta\) by \(1/\vartheta\).  For the separate-pair lower endpoint, the treated-minimum reverse-arc branch uses \((w_0,w_1)=(6064/6935,379/1250)\), \(\vartheta=1/36\), and \(q_1=94711/277400\), while the control-maximum reverse-arc branch uses \((516/625,129/565)\), \(\vartheta=1/36\), and \(q_0=2553/5650\); hence \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=-3461701/31346200\in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9]\).  For the separate-pair upper endpoint, the treated-maximum reverse-arc branch uses \((6736/7565,421/1250)\), \(\vartheta=36\), and \(q_1=212689/302600\), while the control-minimum reverse-arc branch uses \((334/625,167/2495)\), \(\vartheta=36\), and \(q_0=1797/12475\); hence \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=84380923/150997400\in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9]\).  These four separate candidates lie on the same reverse arc and satisfy the same exact active identity and strict inactive inequality.  After eliminating \(z_1,z_0\) and saturating by \(t(1-t)\) and all mixture denominators, let \(g_-\) and \(g_+\) be the primitive square-free degree-sixteen stationary factors for \(\vartheta=1/36\) and \(\vartheta=36\).  Their leading and constant coefficients are respectively \((4404233927002616960449218750000000000,11933213589796668025115770443)\) and \((6602797178337116825836523437500000000000,16287023439341598675579810131)\).  The Sturm-sign strings at the lower box endpoints are \(+--+++-----+-+-++\) and \(---+++-----+-+-++\), giving variation counts \(8\) and \(7\); at the upper box endpoints they are \(-++--+++++--++--+\) and \(+++--+++++--++--+\), giving counts \(7\) and \(6\).  Thus each box isolates one stationary root.  Exact interval subtraction yields \(L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}\in[2934168/10^9,2934170/10^9]\) and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R\in[19313713/10^9,19313715/10^9]\).  \(\mathcal C^\star\) consists of these rational boxes, identities, Sturm data, analytic-branch signs, and interval evaluations showing that every other legal arc, endpoint, corner, and stationary box has a strictly inferior objective value.

definitions.name: Directional tipping-inference handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) starts from cross-fitted asymptotically linear estimators of the finite collection \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\), composes their Gaussian limit with the Hadamard directional derivative of the certified legal-candidate minimum, and inverts a derivative-aware multiplier process for the level set \(L=0\); at stationary continua the handle replaces a finite active set by the support functional of the active semialgebraic set.

statements.statement: For every \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\), the equation \((1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)]m_0-r=0\) has exactly one feasible root \(m_0\in(0,1)\), namely \(m_0=\kappa(r,w,\theta)\); with \(m_1=\theta m_0/\{1+(\theta-1)m_0\}\), it uniquely solves \(r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1\).
statements.justification: This isolates the unique legal branch and prevents denominator-clearing artifacts from entering the global program.
statements.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin derive the corresponding fixed-parameter positive root; the present lemma records the probability-scale root including removable and boundary cases needed by an exact optimizer.
statements.consumer: The endpoint certificate uses this root to reject every algebraic candidate that lies on the wrong mixture branch.

statements.statement: On the strictly positive outcome chart, for fixed \((r,w,\pi)\), \(m_1-m_0\) is strictly increasing in \(\theta\), and \(q-r=(\pi-w)(m_1-m_0)\).  Hence the extrema over \(\theta\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\) occur at \(\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\): if \(\pi-w\geq0\), the lower and upper choices are \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\) and \(\Gamma_a\), while the choices reverse if \(\pi-w\leq0\).
statements.justification: The lemma reduces a continuum of outcome-association choices to two analytic sign branches.
statements.gap: VanderWeele--Arah expose the same bias product, but do not prove endpoint reduction under two-sided odds budgets and a shared posterior pair.
statements.consumer: Applied sensitivity software needs only evaluate the two calibrated outcome-odds endpoints in each branch.

statements.statement: The map \(\operatorname{OR}:(0,1)^2\to(0,\infty)\) has no path-independent continuous extension at \((0,0)\) or \((1,1)\), so \(\theta_{a,x}\) is used only on the strictly positive chart \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  For each \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\), \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\), and the endpoint objectives \(H_x^-\) and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously in \((w_0,w_1)\) to all of the compact region \(D_{A,x}\), including the constant-\(U\) corners.
statements.justification: This separates the interior odds-ratio chart from the compact probability-scale optimization that attains boundary endpoints.
statements.gap: Fixed-parameter binary-confounder calculations do not distinguish the odds-ratio chart from its well-defined probability-scale boundary objectives.
statements.consumer: The sharpness theorem and exact verifier can include null latent cells without assigning an ill-defined boundary odds ratio.

statements.statement: The interior class \(\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) equals the union of the strictly positive Rosenbaum--Rubin binary-logistic full-data families whose treatment coefficient obeys \(|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A\) and whose outcome coefficients obey \(|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a\), with intercepts varying freely subject to the observed margin.  Its closure \(\mathcal M\) is exactly the set of compatible laws in \(\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) satisfying the closed joint-cell inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\); no conditional odds ratio is evaluated at a null cell.
statements.justification: This pins the new bounded class to the published fixed-parameter model rather than introducing an unrelated analogue.
statements.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin specify coefficients tuple by tuple; the bounded union and its probability-table closure are not formulated there.
statements.consumer: Readers can translate familiar logistic sensitivity coefficients directly into the sharp identified-set class.

statements.statement: The ATE identified set over the closed class \(\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R]\), with \(L\) and \(R\) defined by one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  Every endpoint is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M\): at an interior selected pair the law uses the selected feasible risks as conditional Bernoulli marginals and any coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \((X,U)\), while a boundary selected pair is attained as the finite-simplex limit of such strictly positive laws.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), \(\inf\tau=L\), \(\sup\tau=R\), and the closure of the identified set is \([L,R]\); endpoint attainment is asserted there only when an attaining law is itself strictly positive.  When \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x},\theta_{0,x},\theta_{1,x})\) is fixed in the interior chart, the formula reduces exactly to the Rosenbaum--Rubin Section 4 recalculation.
statements.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms must be simultaneously realizable through the same latent confounder.
statements.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin evaluate fixed sensitivity tuples; Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander use distinct exposure-standardization parameters; and Dorn--Guo prove sharpness for a different propensity-only model.  None gives this closed bounded common-binary-\(U\) iff envelope.
statements.consumer: Investigators using interpretable binary-confounder calibrations obtain the narrowest logically valid ATE interval rather than an armwise diagnostic envelope.

statements.statement: For fixed rational \((p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) with interior observed cells and finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) terminates and returns exact real-algebraic representations, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  Its candidate list is exhaustive over both exposure-odds boundary arcs and their endpoints, every legal analytic outcome-sign branch, and all interior stationary points.  It neither admits a cleared-denominator artifact nor omits a legal root, and it handles separately \(\Gamma_A=1\), \(\Gamma_a=1\), constant-\(U\) corners, root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua.  This fixed-input output is not a symbolic atlas over varying observed summaries or budgets.
statements.justification: An exact bound is operational only if every branch and degeneracy has a terminating, auditable certificate.
statements.gap: Existing binary-\(U\) analyses use user-selected grids, and modern marginal-sensitivity bounds use convex duality; neither supplies a complete verifier for this algebraic common-law program.
statements.consumer: A reproducible implementation can attach exact isolating intervals and branch witnesses to reported sensitivity endpoints.

statements.statement: Always \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\), where \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the internal outer relaxation that permits the two arms to use different posterior pairs and is not a published marginal-sensitivity procedure.  For the observed law and budgets in \(P^\star\), the worked exact certificate \(\mathcal C^\star\) gives \(L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9]\), \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=-3461701/31346200\in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9]\), \(R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9]\), and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=84380923/150997400\in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9]\).  Thus both endpoint inequalities are strict, and they remain strict on a relatively open neighborhood of the displayed interior observed law and finite budgets.  The attaining witness itself has \(r_1=53/100\), \(r_0=6/25\), \(\operatorname{OR}(A,U)=16\), \(\theta_1=247/7<36\), \(\theta_0=36\), \(\tau(P^\star)=-1/10\), and nominal contrast \(r_1-r_0=29/100\).
statements.justification: The strict open-set gap demonstrates that common-law compatibility has empirical content beyond a hand-picked numerical coincidence.
statements.gap: The internal armwise relaxation removes only common-posterior compatibility inside the present model.  Dorn--Guo's marginal sensitivity model is generally non-nested and informs the sharpness strategy; no published result isolates this shared-binary-posterior loss under simultaneous treatment and outcome odds budgets.
statements.consumer: Analysts avoid reporting materially overwide intervals that combine mutually incompatible armwise confounder distributions.

statements.statement: For arbitrary real interior observed summaries, \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) admits on every compact finite-budget box \(\mathcal B\) a finite semialgebraic stratification, with defining formulas over the coefficient field \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\); its lower-dimensional strata contain all optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, constant-\(U\) contacts, and stationary continua.  The lower endpoint \(L\) is continuous and coordinatewise nonincreasing in \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  If the observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\) are rational or real algebraic, \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), separately from the fixed-input procedure \(\mathsf{CERT}\), terminates and returns exact quantifier-free sign cells on the complement of \(\mathfrak T_0\) and exact algebraic strata on the surface; rational isolating intervals are returned only after zero-dimensional specialization.
statements.justification: The tipping surface converts three interpretable confounding budgets into the exact frontier at which a positive causal conclusion fails.
statements.gap: Masten--Poirier study breakdown frontiers for other relaxations; the common-\(U\) frontier is multibudget, algebraic, and branch-switching.
statements.consumer: Sensitivity reports can display which combinations of treatment and outcome associations, rather than one arbitrary scalar, overturn the sign conclusion.

statements.statement: If \(\Gamma_A=1\), then \(w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=\pi_x\) for every \(x\), so \(L=R=\sum_x\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x})\).  If \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), then on the strictly positive chart the two joint-cell equalities force \(\mu_{a,0,x}=\mu_{a,1,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every \((a,x)\); continuity of the endpoint objectives gives the same point-identification formula on the closed class.
statements.justification: These reductions are mandatory checks that either absent treatment-confounder association or absent outcome-confounder association removes bias.
statements.gap: The reductions are implicit in fixed-parameter analyses but have not been stated as boundary faces of a sharp bounded envelope.
statements.consumer: They provide unit tests for implementations and an interpretable origin for the tipping atlas.

statements.statement: Let all three budgets diverge and allow a sequence of compatible laws with \(w_{1,x}\to1\), \(w_{0,x}\to0\), \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\), and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\).  Then \([L,R]\) converges to the binary-outcome Manski interval \(\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x\},\;\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x\}\right]\).  No Manski-recovery claim is made at finite budgets or under latent positivity bounded away from zero.
statements.justification: The all-budget limit locates the model between point identification and unrestricted treatment-response bounds without overstating finite-budget coverage.
statements.gap: Imbens relates unrestricted sensitivity to worst-case bounds qualitatively; this proposition gives the exact common-binary-\(U\) endpoint limit and the required loss of latent positivity.
statements.consumer: Users can interpret very large budgets against a familiar worst-case benchmark and detect implementations that converge to the wrong limit.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) be completed into confidence intervals for \((L,R)\) and a simultaneous confidence region for \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with asymptotic coverage uniform over regular branches, finite optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua; and what is the exact directional limit on each singular stratum?
statements.justification: Population sharpness does not by itself quantify sampling uncertainty at the branch switches that define the scientifically relevant frontier.
statements.gap: Zhang--Tchetgen Tchetgen and Nabi et al. treat smooth sensitivity maps, while Fang--Santos gives generic directional theory; none handles this certified algebraic active-set geometry.
statements.consumer: Empirical investigators need coverage statements for the entire set of confounding budgets that preserve a sign conclusion, including near ties.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a fixed population law; identification is the primary target.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with finite \(\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment may depend on \((X,U)\); the candidate full-data law restores conditional ignorability given \((X,U)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed stratum has \(0<p_x<1\); constant-\(U\) boundary laws are retained in the closure, and latent positivity is allowed to vanish only in the all-budget Manski limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell probabilities \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})\) are empirical-frequency estimable; uniform inference through nonsmooth endpoint and level-set maps remains the stated open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed sensitivity parameters, the binary mixtures have unique maximum-likelihood solutions and yield a recalculated average treatment effect.
Quantile balancing gives the sharp ATE interval under the marginal sensitivity model.

For binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome, an exposure-standardization sensitivity function is variation-independent of the observed-data distribution and supports three consistent estimators of marginal causal effects.
General bias formulas specialize to outcome contrasts multiplied by changes in the distribution of a binary confounder.
A sharp joint relative-risk bounding factor applies to an unrestricted unmeasured confounder.
A breakdown frontier is the boundary between assumptions that do and do not support a chosen conclusion.
With no restriction on treatment selection, binary potential-outcome means obey worst-case treatment-response bounds.

tldr: For binary treatment, outcome, and one shared latent binary confounder within finitely many observed strata, the paper characterizes the exact ATE interval over the finite-simplex closure of strictly positive laws satisfying two-sided treatment-confounder and treatment-specific outcome-confounder odds budgets.  Closed joint-cell inequalities define the boundary without assigning a boundary odds ratio.  A unique quadratic-mixture root reduces each outcome budget to two analytic branches; the ATE endpoints then optimize the treated-minus-control contrast over the same posterior pair.  Endpoint-attaining closure laws establish sharpness, a fixed-input exact certificate and a separate parametric algebraic-atlas procedure cover the computational layers, a rational witness proves stable strict tightening over separate armwise pairs, and a piecewise-algebraic zero-tipping surface records where the sign conclusion fails.

project_justification.gap: The original binary-confounder analysis recalculates causal means at fixed parameter tuples, whereas contemporary work studies propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, or exposure-standardized departures from exchangeability.  None of the inspected results optimizes bounded treatment and outcome odds associations while preserving one shared latent posterior pair across both potential-outcome arms and treating the null-cell boundary through the finite-simplex closure.
project_justification.niche: The restriction is scientifically interpretable and algebraically low dimensional, yet it retains compatibility information discarded by separate armwise or arbitrary-\(U\) relaxations.  That combination permits exact endpoints, constructive sharpness, and a multibudget tipping frontier.
project_justification.fill: The iff identified interval is accompanied by a fixed-input exact degeneracy-complete verifier, a separate parametric zero-tipping atlas, a stable strict-gap theorem, point-identification reductions, and the correctly qualified Manski limit.

related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} provide the fixed-tuple binary-mixture inversion recovered by Theorem 1, but do not optimize a bounded region or formulate its finite-simplex closure.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} provide the bias-decomposition identity that motivates the arm-mean map.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} give a variation-independent exposure-standardization sensitivity function and estimators for binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome.  Their sensitivity parameters encode standardized departures from exchangeability and are distinct from one shared binary \(U\) constrained simultaneously by treatment-\(U\) and arm-specific outcome-\(U\) odds budgets; their results neither supply the common-\(U\) sharp envelope and certificate nor automatically sharpen it.  Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} derive a sharp relative-risk factor for arbitrary \(U\), sacrificing the common-binary compatibility used here.  Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} restrict latent treatment odds without companion outcome-\(U\) odds budgets; their optimization and attainability arguments inform this paper.  These published procedures and the common-binary-\(U\) class are generally non-nested, so no numerical dominance comparison is asserted unless an observable-law-dependent budget translation is first proved.  The separate-posterior-pair interval used in Theorem 3 is instead an internal outer relaxation obtained by dropping only the shared-pair constraint.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate inference on assumption frontiers, while Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} supply the adjacent inferential tools for the open sampling problem.  Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
technical_internal_limitation: The worked witness certificate isolates the common lower and upper stationary points, gives exact rational separate-pair extrema, and replaces the floating-point search by rational Sturm data and positive comparison margins.  The remaining technical risks are the fixed-rational-input proof that \(\mathsf{CERT}\) handles every denominator artifact and positive-dimensional stationary continuum outside this worked instance, and the separate parametric-elimination proof for \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\).  Existence of a finite semialgebraic stratification for arbitrary real inputs does not by itself provide rational isolating intervals or an executable symbolic atlas.  This diagnostic is internal and makes no numerical comparison with a published non-nested sensitivity model.
honest_scope: The population formulas, endpoint attainment over the closed finite-simplex class, certificate completeness, strict open-set gap, and tipping stratification are all claims to be proved rather than established facts.  For the strictly positive interior class only the endpoint infimum, supremum, and closure of the identified set are asserted unless an endpoint is separately shown interior.  The odds ratio is never assigned a boundary value; only its probability-scale chart objectives are continuously extended.  Sampling inference at branch ties and stationary continua is deliberately exposed as Open-ended Question 1.  The model assumes a single binary confounder and finite categorical \(X\).  The separate-posterior-pair interval is an internal outer relaxation of this model; the Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander procedure and published arbitrary-\(U\) and marginal sensitivity models are generally non-nested unless an observable-law-dependent translation is established.  Point identification at \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) and the all-budget Manski limit are required sanity reductions.

seed_details.title: Sharp common-binary-confounder ATE envelope and zero-tipping atlas
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Sections 1--4, especially equations (2.1)--(2.4) and (4.3)--(4.7), together with the Appendix
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor proves uniqueness of the positive quadratic-mixture root for a fixed prevalence and fixed log-odds coefficients, then evaluates a finite table.  The first changed step is optimization over a two-sided compact odds region while the two potential-outcome arms retain the same posterior pair for \(U\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing binary latent confounding, bounded treatment and outcome odds ratios, sharp ATE bounds, simultaneous attainability, and tipping surfaces found fixed-grid analyses, arbitrary-confounder bias factors, and propensity-only sensitivity models, but no exact common-\(U\) envelope.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say that this is immediate from Rosenbaum--Rubin because their Section 4 already supplies the quadratic inversion.
seed_details.rebuttal: The inversion is only local in a fixed sensitivity tuple; joint optimization, common-law attainability, degeneracy-complete certification, strict loss from armwise relaxation, and the zero-level budget surface are absent.

seed_details.title: Uniform confidence regions for a branch-switching common-\(U\) tipping surface
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1, the uniform-band construction, and the discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor treats a sensitivity-indexed smooth estimating system.  The first changed step is differentiating a legal-branch minimum over algebraic arc, endpoint, and stationary candidates at optimizer ties and stationary continua.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing directional differentiability, sensitivity endpoints, algebraic optimizer ties, and tipping-set inference found generic directional-bootstrap theory and smooth sensitivity bands, but no common-binary-\(U\) level-set result.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will call this a direct application of Fang--Santos to a finite minimum.
seed_details.rebuttal: The active index is not globally finite before elimination, legal quadratic roots switch, and positive-dimensional stationary sets make the derivative set-valued; those are the unresolved steps.

seed_details.title: Observable-law-dependent translations among binary-odds, marginal-odds, and arbitrary-risk-ratio sensitivity models
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Result 1 and its sharpness construction, Cornfield-threshold section, and Discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor maximizes over an unrestricted confounder on a relative-risk scale.  The first changed step is to retain the shared two-state posterior compatibility equations and solve for necessary and sufficient observable-law-dependent budget translations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sharp translations between binary latent odds budgets, the marginal sensitivity model, and arbitrary-\(U\) relative-risk factors found qualitative comparisons but no equality-case or strict-separation theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say that odds-to-risk conversions give the inclusions by elementary algebra.
seed_details.rebuttal: Baseline risks enter the conversion and the same posterior pair must satisfy both outcome arms, so equality and reverse-inclusion failures require compatibility analysis rather than scalar conversion.

seed_details.title: Sharp joint benefit--harm region under graded common-binary-confounder odds budgets
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--3, symbolic endpoint constructions, and Discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor enumerates response types under unrestricted observational confounding.  The first changed step is a conditional Fr\'echet coupling within each value of \(U\), after the two marginal risks have been selected by the shared posterior-pair quadratic system.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing benefit and harm, a binary unmeasured confounder, treatment-confounder odds budgets, outcome-confounder odds budgets, and sharp joint regions found no graded common-\(U\) result.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say that conditional Fr\'echet bounds can simply be pasted onto the ATE analysis.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coordinatewise conditional extrema need not share the marginal-risk optimizer or one cross-world coupling, so the attainable two-dimensional boundary is not obtained by pasting scalar bounds.

seed_details.title: Sharp aggregate bounds when latent prevalence and log-odds effects are shared across observed strata
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 3, Section 4, and the Appendix discussion of allowing sensitivity parameters to vary by subclass
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor aggregates independently recalculated subclass means.  The first changed step is global optimization when a scientific calibration requires one prevalence or one log-odds coefficient across all strata.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing common sensitivity coefficients across categorical strata with sharp latent-confounder ATE bounds found regression implementations but no semialgebraic sharpness theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will view this as adding equality constraints to the selected seed.
seed_details.rebuttal: The constraints destroy stratumwise separability and create a distinct global compatibility problem, but the gain is narrower and the computational burden is substantially larger.

seed_details.title: Sharp stochastic-dominance and mean-effect bounds for ordinal outcomes with one common binary confounder
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, ordinal response-type programs in Theorems 1--3, and Discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor permits ordinal outcomes but unrestricted confounding.  The first changed step is replacing the Bernoulli quadratic root with a multinomial-odds feasible fiber while maintaining one exposure posterior pair.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing ordinal outcomes, binary latent confounding, bounded outcome odds, and sharp stochastic-dominance bounds found symbolic unrestricted bounds but no graded odds-budget envelope.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say that ordinal outcomes follow by thresholding into binary outcomes.
seed_details.rebuttal: Thresholdwise sharp laws generally do not paste into one ordinal conditional distribution, so simultaneous threshold compatibility is the substantive obstacle.

seed_details.title: Minimax-regret treatment choice under common-binary-confounder sensitivity
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--2 on sharp bounds and simultaneous data compatibility, and Conclusion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor bounds fixed treatment-effect functionals and flags policy values as an extension.  The first changed step is a coupled adversarial optimization of policy welfare over stratum-specific common-\(U\) laws followed by empirical welfare maximization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing common binary confounders, two-sided outcome odds budgets, robust policy learning, and minimax regret found marginal-sensitivity policy work but no common-\(U\) regret frontier.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say that finite categorical \(X\) reduces the policy to choosing the sign of each lower bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds for an unconstrained deterministic policy, so a meaningful version needs capacity or treatment-budget coupling; the extra layer weakens directness for this run.

seed_details.title: Exact minimal joint odds budget needed to overturn an observed sign
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1 and the binary-confounder simplification, and Discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor decomposes bias at fixed sensitivity contrasts.  The first changed step is minimizing a calibrated cost over the full three-budget zero-tipping surface rather than inserting chosen bias components.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for exact joint treatment-odds and arm-specific outcome-odds E-values on the risk-difference scale found scalar bias factors and breakdown frontiers, but not a common-\(U\) three-budget optimum.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will describe the object as a reparameterized point on the selected tipping surface.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is substantially correct unless calibration costs and uniqueness are first-class, so this is retained only as a downstream corollary rather than a kernel.

seed_details.title: Exact law-dependent frontier between propensity-only and common-binary-confounder ATE bounds
seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, loss-minimization identification lemmas, ATE theorem, and Discussion
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor constrains treatment selection but not the association of \(U\) with each potential outcome.  The first changed step is imposing outcome-odds budgets and testing when the propensity-only extremizer admits a common two-state latent representation.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for representability of marginal-sensitivity extremizers by one binary confounder with bounded outcome odds found no necessary-and-sufficient frontier.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will say the models are not nested and hence the comparison is arbitrary.
seed_details.rebuttal: An observable-law-dependent budget translation can make the comparison meaningful, but that translation is itself unresolved and makes this seed less feasible than the direct envelope.

Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander (2022), Theorems 1--2 and Section 3: a variation-independent exposure-standardization sensitivity function and three estimators for binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome, without a shared binary-\(U\) odds-budget envelope.
Dorn and Guo (2023), Theorems 1--2: sharp marginal-sensitivity mean and ATE bounds through simultaneous data compatibility, under a propensity-only model with unrestricted \(U\).
Yadlowsky et al. (2022), identification and ATE sections: loss-based bounds under treatment-selection odds restrictions, without companion outcome-\(U\) budgets.

novelty_justification: The closest historical result is Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983), which identifies the adjusted mean at a user-fixed binary-\(U\) prevalence and fixed treatment and outcome log-odds coefficients.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander (2022) are the closest contemporary binary-exposure and binary-outcome comparator: their exposure-standardization parameters and estimators are variation-independent of the observed law but do not posit one shared binary \(U\) with simultaneous treatment and arm-specific outcome odds budgets.  Dorn and Guo (2023) solve a different propensity-only marginal sensitivity model by quantile balancing.  The proposed kernel instead optimizes the three odds budgets over one common binary posterior pair, proves iff sharpness over the finite-simplex closure by an attaining law, and certifies every algebraic branch and degeneracy.  The common posterior pair is the source of a strict, stable reduction relative to the internal separately optimized armwise relaxation; no nesting or numerical dominance over either published non-nested procedure is claimed.  Targeted searches did not locate an equivalent bounded-parameter envelope in Rosenbaum--Rubin or a later paper.
